title: Re-Write Arithmetic for a Named Non-Owner Policy Reinstated After Nonpayment
content:
**Definition.** On a Named Non-Owner Policy term reinstated after a cancellation for nonpayment, the re-write premium is the nonpayment cancellation return booked on the term multiplied by the re-write days and divided by the days recorded on that return, rounded half up to the cent on the final figure only.

- The re-write days run from the reinstatement effective date, which is included, to the term's expiration date, which is excluded.
- Where two nonpayment cancellation returns share the latest processing date, the one recorded first gives the days.
- A term with no nonpayment cancellation return booked owes no re-write, so nothing is booked.
- The premium is booked as one additional-premium entry for the reinstatement, dated from the reinstatement effective date, with the re-write days as its days.
- A reinstatement without lapse is re-written by the same arithmetic, rounded to the cent.

**Worked example (hypothetical inputs).**

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| nonpayment cancellation return on the ledger | 418.60, recorded with 122 days |
| reinstatement effective date to expiration | 109 days |
| re-write premium | 418.60 multiplied by 109 and divided by 122 = 374.00 |
| entry | dated from the reinstatement effective date, 109 days |

If the ledger shows no nonpayment cancellation return at all, nothing is re-written and no entry is booked.
